source.quote: * **api:** add support for new API version 2026-10-21

tasks.reasoning:
The repo pins @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.39.0 and calls messages.create with model, max_tokens and messages in two places. SDK 1.0.0 is a major release that sends API version 2026-10-21 by default, removes temperature/top_p/top_k and makes MessageParam a union. Nothing breaks today, because old SDKs keep sending 2023-06-01. The upgrade spans many minor releases (0.39 to 1.0), including the OpenTelemetry default in 0.134.0. Response handling was not read by the scan, so the migration agent should also check response-shape usage after the bump. Urgency is low: this is an opt-in upgrade with no forced cutoff announced.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- anthropic:2026-10-21-api-version-2026-10-21 (api-version): New Claude API version 2026-10-21 (anthropic-version header); SDKs older than the new majors keep sending 2023-06-01. The repo's SDK 0.39.0 keeps sending anthropic-version 2023-06-01. Moving to @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.0.0 is what switches the repo to 2026-10-21, so the API-version move is the same edit as the SDK bump.
  Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md
  "This guide lists the code changes for moving from API version `2023-06-01` to `2026-10-21`."
- anthropic:2026-10-21-sampling-params-removed (field-removed): In API version 2026-10-21, temperature, top_p and top_k in Messages and Batch requests return 400. This only bites under API version 2026-10-21, which the 1.0.0 SDK sends. The scanned call sites pass only model, max_tokens and messages, so nothing likely needs changing. The migration agent should confirm that neither api/extract.js nor server.js sets temperature, top_p or top_k, for example through a spread options object.
  Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md
  "In `2026-10-21`, a request that sends `temperature`, `top_p`, or `top_k` returns a 400 error, even at the parameter’s default value."
- anthropic:2026-10-21-document-citations-user-assistant-errors (other): In API version 2026-10-21, document blocks in assistant messages and citations on text blocks in user messages return 400. This only applies under 2026-10-21, which the SDK 1.0.0 upgrade adopts. An invoice scanner likely sends PDF document blocks, but in user messages, which stays valid. The migration agent should check the messages arrays for document blocks in assistant turns and for citations on user text blocks.
  Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md
  "In `2026-10-21`, a request that places a `document` block directly in an `assistant` message returns a 400 error."
- anthropic:2026-10-14-ts-sdk-otel-default (other): TypeScript SDK 0.134.0 auto-creates OpenTelemetry spans and trace headers if a global tracer provider exists (unsure if affects; opt out with openTelemetry:false). Upgrading from 0.39.0 to 1.0.0 passes through 0.134.0, which auto-creates OpenTelemetry spans when a global tracer provider is registered. The migration agent should check whether server.js or the api/ functions register one, and pass openTelemetry:false if spans are unwanted.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "If your app registers a global tracer provider, the SDK will create spans with it after upgrading, and they'll be exported with the rest of your traces."

callSites.why: Calls messages.create through @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.39.0. The 1.0.0 major changes the default API version to 2026-10-21 and turns MessageParam into a union, so the messages construction and types may need adjusting.
Same messages.create call through @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.39.0, which is affected by the 1.0.0 major's API-version default and MessageParam type change.

record.prBody:
## npm @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.0.0 sends API version 2026-10-21 by default; MessageParam becomes a union, temperature/top_p/top_k removed, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry SDKs must move to v1 too [Verified]

### Change

Bumped @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.39.0 -> 1.0.0 via npm (lockfile rewritten). No source changes were needed. Added test/sdk.test.js, which stubs fetch and checks the request/response through the CJS require used by server.js and api/extract.js.

Files touched:
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `test/sdk.test.js`

### Why

SDK 1.0.0 sends anthropic-version 2026-10-21 by default. The repo's two messages.create calls pass only model, max_tokens and messages, so none of the removed or restricted fields are used.

> * **api:** add support for new API version 2026-10-21

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| sdk-test | fail (1) | pass | 0 |
| syntax | pass | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- sdk-test, added by the agent: `node test/sdk.test.js` (fail (1) → pass)
- syntax, added by the agent: `node --check server.js && node --check api/extract.js` (pass → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Test of this change: `sdk-test`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Real API behaviour at 2026-10-21 (only mocked fetch tested)
- Whether the claude-sonnet-4-6 model id is still valid
- npm audit reports 3 vulnerabilities (not examined; multer 1.x is deprecated, unrelated and not upgraded)
- No Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry SDKs, no other-language Anthropic SDKs found in the repo
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- API version header changes from 2023-06-01 to 2026-10-21
- temperature/top_p/top_k: not set anywhere (grepped), so no 400 risk
- Document/citation blocks: the repo only sends image blocks in user messages, so they are unaffected
- OpenTelemetry: no tracer provider is registered in the repo, so no opt-out was needed
- message.content[0].text kept as is (plain JS, no type check); the model replies with a text block first, but a non-text first block would give undefined as before
- SDK license changes from MIT to Apache-2.0

---

preparation.reasoning: Plain Node/Express app with only start and dev scripts. There is no codegen, build, prepare or postinstall step, no workspace packages, and no subfolder project to install. No checks were detected, so nothing needs preparing.

review.summary: The two named call sites (server.js:54 and api/extract.js:54) send only model, max_tokens and messages, with no temperature, top_p or top_k. Both are plain-JS object literals, so the MessageParam union change has no type impact. The PR therefore only needs the dependency bump, and that is what it does. No Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry packages are in package.json. The new test pins the 1.x version and the 2026-10-21 header, and it greps the call sites for sampling params. It runs against a mocked fetch with a text-only message, though. It does not exercise the real image payload, a live 2026-10-21 response, or the deployment runtime. 'verified' is fair for the SDK contract, but live behaviour is unproven.

concerns.issue: Line ~117 (and server.js ~117) reads message.content[0].text and assumes the first block is text. The mock always returns a text block. I could not confirm whether API version 2026-10-21 can put a non-text block first for claude-sonnet-4-6, such as a thinking block or a new block type. If it can, responseText becomes undefined and .match() throws a 500. Check the 2026-10-21 response shape in the API changelog or the SDK's ContentBlock types.

SDK 1.0.0 drops node-fetch, abort-controller and agentkeepalive and relies on the runtime's global fetch, Headers and Response; the test itself uses these globals too. The Node version is not pinned (package.json has no engines field). Confirm the deploy target, which looks like Vercel serverless for api/*.js, runs a Node version 1.0.0 supports. Check the SDK's package.json engines field.

The test sends a text-only content block through a mocked fetch. It does not cover the image/base64 block both call sites actually send, nor whether the 2026-10-21 server accepts it. The upload filter also allows application/pdf to be sent as an 'image' block. That is a pre-existing issue, but worth confirming under the new API version, since it may now be rejected or behave differently.
test/sdk.test.js is added, but there is no "test" script in package.json, so it only runs through the migration agent's harness and not in this repo's own CI or npm test.

The SDK license changes from MIT to Apache-2.0, and the package now adds a bin (anthropic-ai-sdk CLI) and @opentelemetry/api. These are not functional problems, but flag them if license review matters.

checkFirst: Do one live call against the 2026-10-21 API with a real invoice image via /api/extract and confirm content[0] is still a text block with parseable JSON.
Confirm the Node runtime on the deploy target (Vercel/server) satisfies @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.0.0's engines requirement, now that node-fetch is gone.
Check whether claude-sonnet-4-6 is supported under API version 2026-10-21 in the SDK changelog or models docs.
Optionally add "test": "node test/sdk.test.js" to package.json so the check runs in the repo's own CI.
